items.text: The remote control should be designed to be user-friendly for all age groups, including older adults who may struggle with complex interfaces.
The remote control should incorporate an LCD display with menu navigation, similar to mobile phones, to simplify user interaction and reduce the number of physical buttons.
The design should avoid being overly fashionable or metallic, opting instead for lightweight, mouldable plastic to reduce cost and maintain accessibility.
The team will go off to work on individual design tasks during the next half-hour.
Sarah will present a follow-up PowerPoint during the next meeting.
The team will discuss and document the selling price and production cost of the remote control in the shared folder.
The team will consider adding a large print or high-contrast mode for older users to improve readability.
The team will evaluate whether a flip-top design could improve usability and reduce bulk, while considering cost implications.
The remote control should not rely on complex programming or advanced features, ensuring it is usable by non-technical users such as grandads and children.
The product should be accessible to a wide market, including international users, without requiring language-specific adaptations.
The product should avoid the look and feel of traditional remote controls with excessive buttons and unclear labels.
The product should be designed with intuitive, self-explanatory features, such as clear icons and visual menus, to aid understanding across age groups.
